summary: Iteration 3 backend-only testing of LiveKit SFU token minting + AI Debate Coach, plus regression of iteration 1/2 flows. New pytest suite /app/backend/tests/test_livekit_coach.py — 17 tests, 17 PASSED, 0 skipped, 0 failed. Verified: POST /api/livekit/participant-token (401 unauth, 403 non-participant, 404 unknown room, 200 with {server_url, participant_token}; server_url starts with wss://; JWT decoded -> sub='user-test-user-a'/'user-test-user-b', video grant room=<room_id>, roomJoin=true, canPublish=true, canSubscribe=true, exp in future). POST /api/livekit/spectator-token (404 on non-public and unknown room, 200 on public room; JWT sub starts with 'spectator-' and is unique per call, canPublish=false, canSubscribe=true, room=<room_id>). GET /api/public/debates and /api/public/debates/{room_id} now expose side_a.identity/side_b.identity = 'user-<user_id>' and they match the identity embedded in the minted participant token. Debate Coach: two authenticated participants connected to /api/ws/room/{room_id} with an anonymous spectator on /api/ws/watch/{room_id}; 8 provocative/fallacious chat messages (ad hominem, straw man, false dichotomy, whataboutism, appeal to emotion) were sent alternating sides. A {type:'coach', kind, nudge, target, ts} frame WAS delivered to BOTH participant sockets (not a skip) with kind in fallacy|tone|dodge|steelman, non-empty nudge <=200 chars, target in a|b|both, ISO ts. Zero coach frames and zero 'nudge' keys reached the spectator socket (privacy requirement holds). Chat continued to work (all 8 echoes on both participant sockets, all 8 mirrored to spectator as debate-chat). Coach shutdown/restart: after both participants disconnected, a fresh reconnect of the same pair triggered the coach again (round-2 frame received), and no 'Coach loop crash'/Traceback/500 appeared in supervisor backend logs. Edge cases: participant-token with {} -> 404, room_id:null -> 422, body [] -> 422, spectator-token {} -> 404 (no 500s anywhere).

minor.issue: Token TTL is fixed at 30 minutes with no refresh endpoint. A debate longer than 30 min will have participants dropped by the SFU with no way to re-auth other than a full page/room re-join. Consider a refresh route or a longer TTL.

Completely unauthenticated and unthrottled — any caller can mint unlimited subscribe tokens for any public room (each one a billable LiveKit connection). Add rate limiting / captcha or bind to a spectator WS session.

can_publish_data=False for BOTH participants and spectators. If the frontend ever uses LiveKit data channels (e.g. for reactions or the coach transport) it will silently fail; also no can_publish_sources restriction so participants may publish screen share unintentionally.

On the cooldown branch the loop `continue`s WITHOUT resetting self.counters[room_id]; the counter keeps growing so bump_message re-sets the trigger on every subsequent message, causing a tight event->cooldown-skip spin for the remainder of the 15s window (cheap but wasteful). Reset the counter on the cooldown path too.

stop() is only called when hub.rooms[room_id] becomes empty. If exactly one participant stays connected indefinitely the per-room task lives forever polling every 60s (it correctly no-ops on <2 participants, but the task is never reaped). Also no cap on total concurrent coach tasks / no reap on server-side room 'ended'.

Coach nudges are broadcast but never persisted, so a participant who reconnects loses all prior coaching context; also there is no per-room budget on Gemini calls (one LLM call per 5 messages), which is an unbounded cost path for a long/spammy debate.

Still carried over from iteration 2 and NOT fixed: chat items expose 'created_at' while live WS frames use 'ts'; likes use read-then-$inc (stale count under concurrency); published_at never cleared on unpublish; watch WS closes with 4404 before accept() so the code is invisible to browsers (proxy turns it into HTTP 403).

action_items: LOW: reset DebateCoach.counters on the 15s-cooldown continue branch in _loop to avoid an event spin.
LOW: add rate limiting to POST /api/livekit/spectator-token (currently unauthenticated + unbounded token minting for any public room).
LOW: provide a LiveKit token refresh path (or raise TTL) for debates longer than the 30-minute token TTL.

LOW (carry-over from iteration 2, still open): normalize public chat timestamp key to 'ts', use find_one_and_update(return_document=AFTER) for likes, accept() before close(4404) on the watch WS, clear published_at on unpublish.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py is now 1071 lines and holds auth, LLM, matchmaking, rooms, public/watch, two WS hubs AND the coach scheduler + LiveKit token minting — split into routers/services (auth, match, rooms, public, livekit, coach) now; this is the third iteration it has grown unsplit.

DebateCoach and both hubs are per-process in-memory state; with more than one uvicorn worker the coach would start once per worker per room (duplicate Gemini calls and duplicate nudges) and spectator_count would be wrong. Gate on a shared lock/pubsub or document single-worker as a hard constraint.
`import time as _t` appears inline inside _loop and _maybe_intervene — move to module-level imports.
LiveKit grants are minted with can_publish_data=False and no can_publish_sources restriction; make the grant explicit about audio/video-only publishing for participants.

Coach LLM output is trusted after a single json.loads with a broad `except Exception: return`, so malformed model output is silently swallowed at DEBUG level — log at WARNING with the raw payload truncated so intervention failures are diagnosable.
seed_data_creation: Re-seeded test-user-a/test_session_progressive, test-user-b/test_session_traditional and the extra non-participant test-user-c/test_session_third per /app/memory/test_credentials.md. Created one real room via /api/match/enqueue (A then B) with Gemini topics. All rooms, chat_messages, spectator_comments and feedback created by test-user-a/b were deleted after the run and debates/minds_changed counters reset.
test_credentials: Bearer test_session_progressive (test-user-a), Bearer test_session_traditional (test-user-b), Bearer test_session_third (test-user-c non-participant); WS participant channel uses ?token=<same>, spectator WS needs none.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Two suites exist: /app/backend/tests/backend_test.py (iteration 2 watch feature, 22 tests) and /app/backend/tests/test_livekit_coach.py (iteration 3 LiveKit + coach, 17 tests). Both are single-class, order-dependent modules sharing a module-level `state` dict, which works with the pinned pytest.ini `-n 2 --dist loadscope`. pytest-asyncio is NOT installed — async WS tests use asyncio.run() inside sync tests. JWT payloads are decoded with base64.urlsafe_b64decode + padding fix; the LiveKit identity is in the 'sub' claim (NOT 'identity') and grants are under the 'video' claim. The coach DID fire within ~20s of 8 provocative messages in both runs, so the tolerant skip branch was never taken — if a future run skips, it is the probabilistic Gemini decision, not a regression. NOTE: writing files under /app/backend triggers a watchfiles backend reload which kills in-flight coach tasks — write test files first, then run. Frontend (Watch UI, LiveKit video, coach toast) has NEVER been tested by any iteration.
rca_of_the_issue: No functional defects found in the iteration-3 features. All findings are hardening/cost/lifecycle concerns: the unauthenticated spectator-token mint (abuse vector), the fixed 30-min token TTL with no refresh, the coach counter not being reset on the cooldown branch, and per-process coach/hub state that breaks under multiple workers. Iteration-2 minor issues (timestamp key mismatch, stale like count, 4404 close code invisible through the ingress, published_at never cleared) were re-verified as still present.
